cells.tense: You are holding a direction steady right now, and the plan beneath it is solid.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Take the next step on what you have been keeping going, before you have arranged a reason for it. Let it feel right first; the sense can catch up after.
cells.core:
Keeping something lit long enough for a plan to hold weight is the work here. It isn't force. It is the quiet tending that lets the people around a project trust that morning will come, and you can see a step that isn't written down anywhere yet — that seeing is what keeps the rest from going cold.

So take the step. Before your reasons are sorted, do that one thing toward the shape you have been carrying in your head. Skip the check against the plan. One step taken will tell you more about the shape than a week of arranging it would, and the feeling that guided it will turn out to have been information.
cells.sheetLine: You can take a step that isn't written down yet.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get built

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future nobody has handed you, and feeding a fire ahead of its burning.
cells.act: hold the clarity steady and tempered
cells.ask: Hold steady on what is certain about the plan, and add nothing to it this week. Say the same true thing a second time if you have to, and stop there.
cells.core:
Restless arranging is what this looks like from outside: every version of what's coming gets built before it arrives, and the work of building it takes the place of the thing itself. The people near you get the version that is already managed, not the one that is still uncertain, and that gap is where the strain sits.

The next move isn't more preparation. It's standing on the part that is solid and leaving the rest unedited for now. The uncertain parts can stay uncertain through the week; you don't have to close them tonight. What is real holds your weight, and holding that line is the whole of the work.
cells.sheetLine: You are feeding a fire that isn't here yet.

cells.tense: You are standing at a structure you once built, and the fire under it has gone quiet.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Put down one piece of the structure you have been holding that is finished — a duty, a leftover plan, a version of the work. Keep what still serves.
cells.core:
The form is there and the hours are still going, but the thing the form was for has stopped being fed. People used to lean on the direction; now they lean on the shape, and the shape is tired. Staying isn't the same as being there. You can tell the difference if you pause and ask which parts of this you are still choosing.

Some of it is done. Pick one piece — a promise that outlived its season, a plan that already happened, a habit kept past its use — and set it down this week. What's warm stays. Keep warm alone for a few days. The rest will hold when you look up.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding up a structure the fire has left.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get built

cells.tense: You are laying lines for how things get done, and the hand that drew them is filed under circumstance.
cells.act: build the change by persistent work
cells.ask: Give a week of small steady work to the next inch of structure you mean to build — whether or not the week feels like yours.
cells.core:
Order gets made around you and people follow it, and when they ask how it got there you point at the deadline, the situation, whoever needed it. You did decide. The name on it has gone missing, and that is the cost: work you built can feel like something that happened rather than something you set in motion.

Pick one inch. The next piece of shape you mean to build — a routine, a room, a way of working — and spend a week of small steady effort on it. Keep it in view when the week goes badly. You aren't deciding who you are. You are finding your own name on work that was already yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are laying lines you file under circumstance.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get built
